import sys, gzip, math

# Pure NumPy NNLS (Lawson-Hanson active set) with optional scipy fallback.
def nnls_numpy(A, b, tol=1e-10, max_iter=1000):
    A = np.asarray(A, dtype=float)
    b = np.asarray(b, dtype=float).ravel()
    m, n = A.shape
    x = np.zeros(n, dtype=float)
    P = []          # active/passive set (columns kept positive)
    R = list(range(n))
    w = A.T @ (b - A @ x)
    it = 0
    while R and it < max_iter:
        it += 1
        wr = w[R]
        max_w = np.max(wr)
        if max_w <= tol:
            break
        j = R[int(np.argmax(wr))]
        P.append(j)
        R.remove(j)
        # solve unconstrained least squares on active set; guard against empty set
        while True:
            if not P:
                sP = np.array([])
                break
            sP, _, _, _ = np.linalg.lstsq(A[:, P], b, rcond=None)
            if np.all(sP > tol):
                break
            # move from current x toward the unconstrained solution
            xs = x[P]
            neg = sP <= tol
            if not np.any(neg):
                break
            # alpha = min over negative components of xs/(xs - sP)
            candidates = xs[neg] / (xs[neg] - sP[neg] + 1e-300)
            alpha = np.min(candidates)
            x[P] = xs + alpha * (sP - xs)
            # remove zeroed active variables
            zero = np.where(x[P] <= tol)[0]
            if len(zero) == 0:
                break
            for k in sorted(zero, reverse=True):
                R.append(P[k])
                del P[k]
            if not P:

                break
        if P:

    # clip tiny negative values
    x = np.clip(x, 0.0, None)
    return x
